raw:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "category": "domain_extent",
      "entity": "cantilever design domain",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1.1 refers the design domain to Fig. 3 left, but supplies no dimensions or cross-section proportions. Absolute dimensions matter because the filter radius is fixed at 0.1 m. For the alternatives below, x is the span direction, with dimensions L, H, W along x, y, z.",
      "readings": [
        "Rectangular domain L=3 m, H=1 m, W=1 m.",
        "Rectangular domain L=6 m, H=1 m, W=1 m.",
        "Rectangular domain L=3 m, H=1 m, W=0.5 m.",
        "Rectangular domain L=0.3 m, H=0.1 m, W=0.1 m."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "support_location_extent",
      "entity": "built-in root of the cantilever",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "The word cantilever indicates a built-in support, but Sec. 6.1.1 gives no supported surface, patch, edge, or node set. Taking the root as x=0 does not determine the extent of its clamp.",
      "readings": [
        "Fix all three displacement components at every node on the entire x=0 face.",
        "Fix all three displacement components only along the perimeter edges of the x=0 face.",
        "Fix all three displacement components on the central root patch y/H and z/W between 0.25 and 0.75."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_position",
      "entity": "cantilever external load location",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1.1 gives no load coordinates or loaded boundary set. Its reference to [64] supplies no usable loading information within the provided text.",
      "readings": [
        "Free-end face center: (x/L,y/H,z/W)=(1,0.5,0.5).",
        "Center of the lower free-end edge: (1,0,0.5).",
        "Lower free-end corner: (1,0,0).",
        "Near-tip location on the lower surface: (0.9,0,0.5)."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_extent_distribution",
      "entity": "spatial distribution and nodal assembly of the external load",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1.1 specifies neither a concentrated force nor a line, surface, or patch load, and provides no nodal force weights.",
      "readings": [
        "Concentrated force at one node.",
        "Uniform line load across the lower free-end edge, assembled with consistent endpoint half weights.",
        "Equal nodal forces at every node on the lower free-end edge, including its endpoints.",
        "Uniform traction on the entire free-end face.",
        "Uniform traction on a central free-end patch with y/H and z/W between 0.4 and 0.6."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_direction",
      "entity": "cantilever external force direction",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "No force direction is stated in Sec. 6.1.1. The x- and y-direction loads in Sec. 6.1.2 belong to the blade example.",
      "readings": [
        "Transverse force in the negative y direction.",
        "Transverse force in the negative z direction.",
        "Axial force in the positive x direction.",
        "Oblique transverse force proportional to (0,-1,-1)."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_magnitude",
      "entity": "common amplitude of the cantilever loading",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1.1 gives no force or traction magnitude. This item concerns a common multiplier with the load pattern and relative load-case weights held fixed.",
      "readings": [
        "Total resultant force of 1 N.",
        "Total resultant force of 10 N.",
        "Total resultant force of 1000 N."
      ],
      "effect": "scale_only"
    },
    {
      "category": "other",
      "entity": "number of load cases and compliance aggregation",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1.1 does not explicitly give the number of load cases or an aggregation rule. Sec. 2 defines compliance for one right-hand side; the explicit two-case average in Sec. 6.1.2 applies to the blade.",
      "readings": [
        "One load case, minimizing its compliance.",
        "Two independently solved load cases, minimizing their equal-weight mean compliance.",
        "Two independently solved load cases, minimizing 0.75 times the first compliance plus 0.25 times the second."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "volume_fraction",
      "entity": "meaning and normalization of the constraint bound 0.5",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1.1 calls 0.5 an upper bound for mass without units or normalization. Eq. (1) instead defines an absolute volume bound through the sum of element volumes multiplied by design densities.",
      "readings": [
        "A normalized material-volume fraction of 0.5 of the full design domain.",
        "An absolute material-volume bound v_u=0.5 m^3.",
        "An absolute mass bound of 0.5 kg, converted to a volume bound using solid mass density."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "passive_region",
      "entity": "non-design regions near the support and load",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Neither Sec. 6.1.1 nor the general formulation identifies passive cells, their extent, or whether fixed-solid regions are enforced before or after filtering.",
      "readings": [
        "No passive cells; every domain element is designable.",
        "A one-element-thick root layer is fixed solid.",
        "A one-element-thick pad adjacent to the loaded boundary is fixed solid.",
        "Root and load pads have design density mu=1 and participate in the Helmholtz filter.",
        "Root and load pads have physical density rho=1 enforced after filtering."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "material",
      "entity": "solid Young's modulus",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1.1 prints the modulus as 2.0 times 10^{1}1 N/m^2, leaving the final 1 outside the exponent.",
      "readings": [
        "E_0=2.0e11 Pa, interpreting both digits 1 as the exponent 11.",
        "E_0=20 Pa, taking the displayed exponent as 1 and treating the trailing 1 as multiplication or a transcription artifact."
      ],
      "effect": "scale_only"
    },
    {
      "category": "material",
      "entity": "solid mass density, conditional on an absolute mass interpretation",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "No solid mass density is supplied. It is needed to convert a literal mass limit in Sec. 6.1.1 into the volume constraint required by the requested solver; it is unnecessary for a normalized volume-fraction interpretation.",
      "readings": [
        "Solid mass density of 1 kg/m^3.",
        "Solid mass density of 1000 kg/m^3.",
        "Solid mass density of 7800 kg/m^3."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Helmholtz filter boundary conditions",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Eq. (3) specifies the differential operator and Sec. 6.1.1 specifies its radius, but neither supplies boundary conditions.",
      "readings": [
        "Homogeneous Neumann conditions on every exterior boundary.",
        "Homogeneous Dirichlet conditions rho=0 on every exterior boundary.",
        "Dirichlet rho=1 on support and load boundaries, with homogeneous Neumann conditions elsewhere."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "discrete Helmholtz filter and density transfers",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Eq. (3) gives a continuous filter. Sec. 6.1.1 does not specify its discrete mass matrix or how elementwise mu is transferred to the filter space and filtered rho back to elements.",
      "readings": [
        "Q1 nodal finite-element filter with a consistent mass matrix, weak assembly of the elementwise source, and element-average rho for SIMP.",
        "Q1 nodal finite-element filter with a row-sum-lumped mass matrix, volume-weighted element-to-node averaging, and nodal averaging back to elements."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "numerical accuracy of the Helmholtz filter solve",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1.1 reports elastic-solve parameters but does not separately identify the filter linear solver or its stopping tolerance.",
      "readings": [
        "Direct factorization of the discrete Helmholtz system.",
        "Iterative filter solve to relative residual 1e-10.",
        "Iterative filter solve to relative residual 1e-4."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "structured-grid element counts along each axis",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1.1 supplies total design-variable counts and uniform first-order hexahedra, but no directional element counts, element aspect ratios, or refinement mapping. The following alternatives all reproduce the three stated totals for a fully designable brick.",
      "readings": [
        "(Nx,Ny,Nz)=(30,10,10), then (60,20,20), then (120,40,40).",
        "(Nx,Ny,Nz)=(50,10,6), then (100,20,12), then (200,40,24).",
        "(Nx,Ny,Nz)=(20,15,10), then (40,30,20), then (80,60,40)."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "hexahedral element integration and stabilization",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "First-order hexahedra are specified in Sec. 6.1.1, but their stiffness quadrature and any reduced-integration stabilization are not.",
      "readings": [
        "Fully integrated Q1 hexahedra with 2x2x2 Gauss quadrature.",
        "One-point reduced-integration Q1 hexahedra with hourglass stabilization.",
        "Selective reduced integration of the volumetric stiffness contribution."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "initial design-density field",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1.1 does not report the initial design. This matters for the nonconvex SIMP problem; the discussion of Table 1 explicitly reports different local minima.",
      "readings": [
        "Uniform initial design density mu=0.5.",
        "Uniform initial design density mu=0.25.",
        "Initial density mu=0.6 in the root half and mu=0.4 in the tip half."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "IPOPT Hessian, barrier, and scaling configuration",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1.1 names IPOPT and its convergence threshold, but does not identify Hessian treatment, barrier strategy, or problem scaling.",
      "readings": [
        "Exact Lagrangian Hessian, monotone barrier strategy, and no problem scaling.",
        "Limited-memory BFGS Hessian approximation, adaptive barrier strategy, and gradient-based scaling."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "PCG absolute tolerance and iteration limit",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Algorithm 5 requires epsilon_abs and N_maxit, but Sec. 6.1.1 provides neither. The stated relative tolerance does not determine these settings.",
      "readings": [
        "epsilon_abs=0 and N_maxit=1000.",
        "epsilon_abs=1e-12 and N_maxit=10000."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "HYPRE AMG configuration",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Secs. 5.2 and 6 identify HYPRE AMG, but do not specify its cycle, smoothing configuration, or coarsening settings.",
      "readings": [
        "V-cycle AMG with one weighted-Jacobi smoothing sweep before and after coarse correction.",
        "W-cycle AMG with two symmetric Gauss-Seidel smoothing sweeps before and after coarse correction."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    }
  ]
}

items.entity: cantilever design domain
items.description: Sec. 6.1.1 refers the design domain to Fig. 3 left, but supplies no dimensions or cross-section proportions. Absolute dimensions matter because the filter radius is fixed at 0.1 m. For the alternatives below, x is the span direction, with dimensions L, H, W along x, y, z.
readings: Rectangular domain L=3 m, H=1 m, W=1 m.
Rectangular domain L=6 m, H=1 m, W=1 m.
Rectangular domain L=3 m, H=1 m, W=0.5 m.
Rectangular domain L=0.3 m, H=0.1 m, W=0.1 m.

readings: Fix all three displacement components at every node on the entire x=0 face.
Fix all three displacement components only along the perimeter edges of the x=0 face.
Fix all three displacement components on the central root patch y/H and z/W between 0.25 and 0.75.
